{"id": "tooluse_ngnzxMF41XHKeEramsasbY", "content": "[{'text': '## Documentation search results\\n\\n{\"content\":{\"result\":[{\"rank_order\":1,\"title\":\"ADVCOST05-BP06 Use provisioned throughput for steady-state agents and on-demand pricing for variable workloads\",\"context\":\"## Implementation guidance\\\\n\\\\nAmazon Bedrock has three pricing models for inference: on-demand\\\\n(pay per token with no commitment), Provisioned Throughput\\\\n(reserved capacity at a lower per-token rate with time-based\\\\ncommitment), and batch inference (lowest per-token rate for\\\\nasynchronous, latency-tolerant workloads). If you pick the wrong\\\\nmodel for an agent\\'s pattern, you risk overpaying either through\\\\nidle reserved capacity or through premium on-demand rates on\\\\nsteady-state volume.\\\\n\\\\nThe break-even calculation for Provisioned Throughput compares the\\\\ncommitted hourly rate against what the same invocation volume\\\\nwould cost on-demand. Agents with consistent, predictable volume\\\\nthat exceeds this threshold (brand safety monitors running around\\\\nthe clock and constant content classification) benefit from\\\\nProvisioned Throughput. Agents with spiky, unpredictable patterns\\\\n(campaign planning that surges during launch cycles and seasonal\\\\ncreative generation) typically cost less on-demand because the\\\\nidle hours during low-demand periods would waste reserved\\\\ncapacity. Provisioned Throughput is available with no commitment\\\\n(hourly), 1-month, or 6-month terms. Teams can start with the\\\\nno-commitment option to validate utilization before locking into\\\\nterm discounts.\\\\n\\\\nBatch eligibility depends on whether a workload can be deferred.\\\\nIf an inference consumer reads the result hours after it is\\\\nproduced, it is paying for an unused low-latency guarantee.\\\\nAmazon Bedrock batch inference prices that difference by queuing\\\\nrequests and processing them when capacity is available, at lower\\\\nper-token rates.\\\\n\\\\nThe completion window for batch inference is a range, not a\\\\nguaranteed deadline. A downstream consumer that assumes a fixed\\\\ncompletion time treats an occasional slow batch as a missing-data\\\\nincident. Batch jobs can\\'t support conversational or tool-calling\\\\ninteractions, so a workflow that mixes deferrable analysis with\\\\ninteractive steps must be split at that boundary.\\\\n\\\\nAction group functions on\\\\nAWS Lambda are a separate cost that compounds with inference\\\\ncosts. Each agent invocation might trigger multiple Lambda calls\\\\nfor tool use (such as database lookups, API calls, and\\\\ncalculations). Lambda charges for both invocation count and\\\\nduration multiplied by allocated memory. Over-provisioned memory\\\\nincreases cost without reducing execution time when the function\\\\nis I/O-bound rather than compute-bound.\\\\nAWS Lambda Power Tuning tests memory configurations to find the\\\\npoint where additional memory stops improving performance, the\\\\nminimum cost\\\\n\\\\n*[truncated \u2014 additional content omitted]*\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/video-streaming-advertising-lens/advcost05-bp06.html\"},{\"rank_order\":2,\"title\":\"How to estimate Amazon Bedrock costs for public sector applications | AWS Public Sector Blog\",\"context\":\"### Inference\\\\n\\\\nWhen you submit an input to an FM, the model predicts a probable sequence of tokens and returns that sequence as the output. This is known as inference. Amazon Bedrock provides you the capability of running inference with the FM of your choice. Therefore, model inference is the primary driver for costs incurred with Amazon Bedrock. There are different options available for inference, and pricing can vary across these different types:\\\\n\\\\n* **On-Demand** \u2013 With this option, you get maximum flexibility since you only pay for what you use, without any long-term commitments. When using text models, you\u2019re charged based on the tokens processed \u2013 both for input and output. For embedding models, you just pay for input tokens processed. If you\u2019re generating images, the charge is per image.\\\\n* **Batch processing** \u2013 In batch processing, you submit multiple requests in a single input file and get all responses in one output file. These results are stored in your Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) bucket for easy access later. Batch mode costs 50 percent less than On-Demand mode for select AI models from providers like Anthropic, Meta, Mistral AI, and Amazon.\\\\n* **Provisioned Throughput** \u2013 With Provisioned Throughput allows you to purchase dedicated model units for your specific base or custom models where you get throughput when you need it most. Each model unit purchased provides a specific throughput capacity, measured by the maximum number of tokens (both input and output) that can be processed per minute. The pricing follows an hourly charging model with added discounts for commitments.\\\\n* **Prompt caching** \u2013 Prompt caching in Amazon Bedrock adds portions of your context to a cache. The model can use the cache to skip recomputation of inputs and reduce input token processing cost as well as latency. When using prompt caching, you\u2019re charged at a reduced rate for tokens read from cache. Depending on the model, however, tokens written to cache might be charged at a rate that is higher than that of uncached input tokens.\\\\n* **Latency-optimized inference** \u2013Latency-optimized inference in Amazon Bedrock delivers significantly faster response times for FM without compromising accuracy. Developers can set the \u201cLatency\u201d parameter to \u201coptimized\u201d in the Amazon Bedrock runtime API to access this capability. For pricing details, check each model\u2019s pricing for latency-optimized inference\",\"url\":\"https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/publicsector/how-to-estimate-amazon-bedrock-costs-for-public-sector-applications/\"},{\"rank_order\":3,\"title\":\"Amazon Bedrock\",\"context\":\"### Pricing model\\\\n\\\\nAmazon Bedrock offers flexible pricing based on API consumption. Organizations pay for input and output tokens processed during on-demand usage, or they can use and scale imported FMs measured in capacity units.\\\\n\\\\nBedrock exposes four inference service tiers \u2014 **Reserved**, **Priority**, **Standard**, and **Flex** \u2014 that let a workload trade off availability, latency, and cost without changing models or APIs. Three of them (Priority, Standard, Flex) are on-demand and share a single per-model quota; tier selection is just a request-time parameter. The fourth (Reserved) is a separate pool with its own SLA and minimum commitment. This sits alongside Bedrock\\'s other capacity controls \u2014 Provisioned Throughput for custom and imported models, batch inference, and cross-region inference \u2014 and is usually the first lever to reach for on shared on-demand models\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/gen-ai-inference-architecture-and-best-practices-on-aws/amazon-bedrock.html\"}]}}\\n\\n## Recent AWS announcements (What\\'s New)\\n\\nNewer than your training data may be. When these conflict with the documentation results above or with what you remember, prefer the most recent dated source.\\n\\n{\"content\":{\"result\":[{\"rank_order\":1,\"title\":\"Amazon Bedrock introduces Priority and Flex inference service tiers - AWS\",\"context\":\"Amazon Bedrock, a service offered by AWS, has introduced two new inference service tiers: Flex and Priority. The Flex tier is designed for non-interactive workloads that can tolerate longer latencies, making it suitable for model evaluations, content summarization, labeling and annotation, and multistep agentic workflow. It is priced at a discount relative to the Standard tier but receives lower priority during periods of high demand. The Priority tier, on the other hand, is ideal for mission-critical applications, real-time end-user interactions, and interactive experiences where consistent, fast responses are essential. During periods of high demand, Priority requests receive processing priority over other service tiers at a premium price. These new service tiers are available for leading foundation models like OpenAI (gpt-oss-20b, gpt-oss-120b), DeepSeek (DeepSeek V3.1), Qwen3 (Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct, Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct, 32B dense, Qwen3-235B-A22B-2507), and Amazon Nova (Nova Pro and Nova Premier).
